title: Course Schedule II
summary: Return an order in which to take all the courses so that every prerequisite comes first, or [] if none exists.

tests.explain: 0 has no prerequisites, so it goes first. 1 and 2 each need only 0, and 3 needs both. [0, 2, 1, 3] is just as correct.
0 and 1 each need the other, so neither can be first: return [].
With no prerequisites any order of 0, 1 and 2 works.

hints: Any order where each prerequisite comes before the course that needs it is accepted. That is a topological order of the graph pre → course.
Kahn's algorithm builds one: queue every course with in-degree 0, and each time you take a course, lower the in-degree of the courses it unlocks and queue the ones that reach 0.
The order in which courses leave the queue is the answer. If it has fewer than numCourses entries, some courses are stuck on a cycle: return [].

complexity.time: O(V + E): each course and each pair is processed once
complexity.space: O(V + E): the adjacency list, in-degrees and queue
